assertion_conditions: The reasoning content corresponds traceably to the specific prior observation, repeating its result such as a downloaded state, returned status codes, environment facts, or pass/fail verdicts.
The restatement may distinguish which checks passed from those that failed.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only proposes future steps without characterizing a prior result.
The reasoning is merely topically related to the observation without restating its outcome.
The reasoning draws only on prior knowledge or the user request rather than on the observation's result.

accepted_predicates.name: DERIVES_NEXT_ACTION_FROM_OBSERVATION
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning adopts a concrete next action because of a finding in a prior observation, using that finding as the stated basis for the choice.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text that selects an approach in light of the observation.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The prior tool result supplying the deciding information.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning explicitly links a specific finding of the observation, such as an unavailable utility, available package, error cause, or test result, to the concrete step it decides to take.
The decided step would plausibly differ had the observation reported a different finding.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning restates the result without using it to select a step.
The chosen step was already fixed before the observation and is not justified by it.
The link is only topical or temporal, with no stated dependence of the chosen step on the observation.

accepted_predicates.name: DELIBERATES_ON_AMBIGUOUS_REQUIREMENT
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning identifies a requirement detail that admits multiple readings and weighs competing interpretations before committing to one behavior.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text containing the interpretative deliberation.

assertion_conditions: At least one under-specified requirement detail is explicitly called out as ambiguous.
At least two candidate behaviors are considered, with a rationale for the one finally adopted.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning merely lists implementation steps for an unambiguous requirement.
The reasoning states an assumption without weighing alternatives.
The ambiguity is noted but no behavior is selected.

accepted_predicates.name: CREATES_FILE_ARTIFACT
accepted_predicates.definition: The action persists content at a named filesystem path, producing a durable artifact such as a source file, script, or other content file that later steps can execute, import, or serve.
assertion_conditions: The invocation supplies both content to persist and a target path where it is written.
The persisted artifact is intended for subsequent use in the workflow rather than discarded immediately.
exclusion_conditions: The content is passed inline to an interpreter and no durable file artifact is produced.
The invocation only reads, lists, or inspects existing paths.
The invocation is rejected before any content is written.

accepted_predicates.name: EXECUTES_PREVIOUSLY_CREATED_ARTIFACT
accepted_predicates.definition: The action runs the filesystem artifact produced by an earlier file-creating action, so the execution depends on that earlier artifact's content.

parameters.name: execution_action
parameters.description: The action that invokes the artifact.

parameters.name: creation_action
parameters.description: The earlier action that wrote the artifact to its path.

assertion_conditions: The creation action precedes the execution action and writes to a specific path.
The execution command references that same path, so the executed content is the artifact produced by the creation action.
exclusion_conditions: The executed file was produced by some other means than the creation action.
The later action only inspects or edits the artifact without running it.
The execution invokes a different path or a copy not traceable to the creation action.

accepted_predicates.name: LAUNCHES_DETACHED_LONG_RUNNING_SERVICE
accepted_predicates.definition: The action starts a long-running server process detached from the invoking shell, with its output redirected, so the process keeps running after the call returns.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The invocation that starts the service in the background.

assertion_conditions: The command detaches the process from the calling shell and redirects its output to a log or equivalent sink.
The invocation reports a process identifier or otherwise acknowledges the detached start.
exclusion_conditions: The server is started in the foreground and blocks the invocation.
The command runs a short-lived operation expected to finish within the call.
The process is started without detachment or output redirection.

accepted_predicates.name: PROBES_DEPLOYED_SERVICE_ENDPOINT
accepted_predicates.definition: The action sends one or more crafted requests to the HTTP endpoint of an already running service, and the resulting observation records the returned status codes and response bodies for those requests.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action issuing the requests to the live endpoint.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The tool result recording the returned statuses and payloads.

assertion_conditions: The requests target the deployed service over the network rather than importing its code in-process.
The payloads are constructed to exercise the endpoint, including valid inputs and/or invalid-input cases intended to produce error statuses.
The observation reports the returned status code and body for at least one issued request.
exclusion_conditions: The action only starts or inspects the process without sending requests.
The invocation fails before any request reaches the service, so no response is recorded.
The action targets a different endpoint or a service that is not running.

accepted_predicates.name: VERIFIES_REACHABILITY_VIA_EXTERNAL_INTERFACE
accepted_predicates.definition: The action addresses the deployed service through a non-loopback network address, and the observation's successful response confirms that the service is bound to all interfaces rather than localhost only.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The action contacting the service through the non-loopback address.

parameters.name: observation
parameters.description: The tool result reporting the response obtained over that address.

assertion_conditions: The request URL or host used by the action is a non-loopback address of the service host.
The observation reports a successful response from that address, establishing external reachability.
exclusion_conditions: The request is sent only to the loopback address, which cannot distinguish all-interfaces binding from localhost-only binding.
The attempt over the non-loopback address fails or returns no response.
The service is not running or the address does not belong to the service host.

accepted_predicates.name: ALLOCATES_EXTENDED_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT
accepted_predicates.definition: The action explicitly assigns an extended execution time budget to an invocation anticipated to take nontrivial time, such as a remote artifact download, a first-time model load, a service warm-up, or a network probe.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: The invocation carrying the extended time budget.

assertion_conditions: The invocation's arguments include an explicit timeout or time-budget setting.
The invoked command involves work that can reasonably take nontrivial time, such as bulk downloading, model loading, sleeping for warm-up, or network requests.
exclusion_conditions: No explicit timeout is set and the invocation relies on the environment default.
The timeout is set for a command expected to complete instantly with no anticipated delay.
The timeout value is present but the command does not involve the long-running work it is meant to accommodate.
